246748812_5d514559.text: Both endogenous orexins (orexin-A and orexin-B) are produced by a subpopulation of neurons exclusively located in the lateral hypothalamus (LH) (Sakurai, 2014) . Axonal projections from these cells extend throughout the central nervous system to both the brain (Peyron et al., 1998) and spinal cord (Pol, 1999) , illustrating the anatomical basis for the involvement of orexin signaling in a broad range of neural functions (Sakurai, 2014)(Peyron et al., 2017) . Ongoing studies are revealing notable roles for orexin signals in regulating arousal and emotional states (including human panic attacks (Johnson et al., 2009) ) as well as risk-taking, reward perception and decision-making (Blomeley et al., 2017)(Giardino et al., 2018)(Mahler et al., 2014) . Furthermore, orexin cell activity in vivo is rapidly modulated by diverse external cues (Giardino et al., 2018)(González et al., 2016)(Mileykovskiy et al., 2005) and slowly modulated by internal body state via nutrient-sensing (Burdakov et al., 2006)(Karnani et al., 2011) , suggesting that the orexin system may couple internal and external sensations to brain states and actions.
